static_traits.name: Li Jin
static_traits.social_status: Relationship tension with friends and family after divorce; having one close friend's support, but not yet discussing negative thinking with them.
static_traits.medical_history: No obvious physical illness; no similar problems before; no prior psychotherapy/counseling history.
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, strong logic, good cooperativeness; able to identify and describe automatic thoughts; anxious emotions; speech rate not mentioned.

basic_info.main_problem: I am writing an ebook about animals, but I always dismiss my efforts, believing anyone can do this and it does not require intelligence. These thoughts appeared since I started writing, especially more pronounced when facing writing challenges; I believe the stress of divorce triggered these thoughts, and they come more frequently when comparing with other authors. Almost every time I sit down to write or brainstorm, these dismissive thoughts appear; I tried pushing them away, but they keep recurring.
basic_info.core_demands: I sought counseling because these negative thoughts hinder my progress in writing an e-book and affect my self-esteem.
growth_experiences: Recently experienced divorce, leading to relationship tension with friends and family (interpersonal relationships frustrated).

A few weeks ago the pet dogs went missing for a few hours, and I immediately thought of the worst-case scenarios (they had died or were lost forever). Although they were eventually found, since then whenever I cannot see them I panic and imagine terrible outcomes, with worry occupying almost the whole day; I canceled plans with friends to stay home and watch them, frequently contacted animal shelters, posted lost-dog notices, and my sleep and diet were affected.

special_situations.event: When sitting down to write or brainstorming for an e-book
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If anyone can write an ebook and it does not require intelligence, then my efforts have no value, showing I am not smart
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Belittling and dismissing my own progress and strengths, trying to push these thoughts away but they keep recurring
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Writing books does not require intelligence; anyone can do it; my efforts are nothing

special_situations.event: When comparing oneself with other authors
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am inferior to other authors, it proves I am not smart enough and do not deserve to be called an author
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly compares and questions one's own ability and worth

special_situations.event: When encountering challenges or blocks in the writing process
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I encounter difficulty it equals I am not smart enough and I will fail
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to repress negative thoughts, but becoming more self-denying when facing difficulties
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot do it / I am not smart enough

special_situations.event: When I cannot see the dogs or recall the previous experience of the dogs going missing
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot monitor and control at all times, the worst will happen
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Canceling social plans to stay home and keep watch, frequently contacting the shelter, posting notices, putting protection on the residence
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They may have gotten into trouble; I may never see them again

core_conflict.wish: Longs for their ability to be affirmed, and to ensure the safety and controllability of significant objects (pets)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being dismissed and failing; fearing losing loved ones and uncontrollable disasters happening
defense_goal: Avoids evaluation pressure and the sense of failure by belittling positive achievements
Gains a sense of safety by maintaining high vigilance and control

object_relations.self_representation: Not smart enough, a self needing constant self-proof
object_relations.object_representation: Others / the writer community are superior and judgmental reference standards

object_relations.self_representation: An anxious guardian, one who must prevent disasters at all times
object_relations.object_representation: The external world (especially pet-related) is dangerous and unpredictable

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor discusses evidence, inviting balance between vigilance and reassurance, or talking about uncertainty over pet safety
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Only by staying highly vigilant and preparing in advance for every 'what if' can I be responsible and ensure safety
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding by listing potential risks and coping plans, frequently using 'what if / if' expressions, in a cautious tone, slightly anxious, emphasizing the need for more control.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When affirmed by others for writing progress or invited to attend to one's own positive efforts
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Positive feedback 'does not count', because 'anyone can do this, it does not require intelligence'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Attributing achievements to 'this is simple / luck / does not require ability' in a calm, objective tone, to reduce emotional involvement and the pressure of being evaluated.

manifestations: Recently divorced, leading to relationship tension with friends and family
Although there are supportive close friends, not yet sharing my negative thinking and distress
outcomes: Subjective sense of isolation and insufficient support

manifestations: Belittling my writing efforts as 'not requiring intelligence, anyone can do it'
Finds it hard to acknowledge invested effort and progress
outcomes: Reduced self-esteem and sense of worth

manifestations: Strongly pursuing absolute certainty and control over pet safety
Difficulty tolerating uncertainty (persistent 'if / what if' worries)
outcomes: Over-monitoring and avoidance shrink the life scope

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeated Self-denial and belittling achievements ('anyone can do this, it does not require intelligence')
Finds it hard to accept positive evidence and affirming feedback

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Cancels plans with friends and instead uses energy on monitoring and caring for the pet at home
Repressing urges to go out socially / seek help, turning into self-tension and self-depletion

positive_force: Has initiative and takes multiple concrete safety measures to protect the pet (leash, reinforcing the environment, etc.)
Willing to seek psychological counseling to change thinking patterns
Able to identify and name own cognitive biases (e.g. dismissing the positive)
Has a stable job and basic life structure
negative_force: Strong catastrophizing and 'what if' thinking, finding it hard to tolerate uncertainty
Dismissing the positive and comparing with others leading to low self-esteem, weakening self-efficacy
Excessive monitoring and avoidance behaviors maintaining anxiety (canceling plans, continuous checking)
Rigid need for absolute control and certainty
Available social support not yet fully utilized (not yet sharing distress with friends)

target_behavior.behavior: Intense anxiety and excessive monitoring about pet safety
antecedent: When I cannot see the dogs
Recalling the dog getting lost a few weeks ago
target_behavior.core_reason: A recent getting-lost incident formed a conditioned fear memory, accompanied by catastrophizing cognitions and a strong need for certainty
target_behavior.function: Avoiding uncertainty, gaining brief reassurance and a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Canceling plans with friends, sleep and diet affected, persistent anxiety affecting work focus

target_behavior.behavior: Self-deprecation and dismissing the positive in writing situations (Self-denial automatic thoughts)
antecedent: When sitting down to write or brainstorm
When writing hits a challenge or gets stuck
When comparing oneself with other authors
target_behavior.core_reason: Stress from divorce triggering Self-doubt; equating difficulties with inadequacy and forming the 'dismissing the positive' cognitive pattern
target_behavior.function: Temporarily reduces the pressure of being evaluated and failing (lowering expectations, avoiding vulnerability)
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased writing motivation and focus, blocked progress, impaired self-esteem
